answer: Reputation-weighted task assignment: each identity's queue share is set by verified completions, so fresh accounts receive only low-value work. A sonnet of checks—delayed payout, peer review, and random audit—raises the effort per fake identity above its expected yield. Isolated clusters, like a lagoon cut off from the main flow, never accumulate enough history to bid on high-value tasks. An attacker must fund sustained genuine labor across a wide dune of accounts before any single one earns real capacity, making the marginal cost of each additional sybil exceed its marginal revenue.
